messages:
maria: Quick follow-up from today's RFC review — wanted to capture a few concrete tradeoffs we agreed on for the continuous-batcher refactor and a proposed next-step plan.

alex: SGTM. Can you bullet the tradeoffs? I'm still fuzzy on eviction vs backpressure ordering.

maria: short list: 1) admission backpressure (drop/slowdown) vs eviction (preempt and requeue) for tail-latency tenants, 2) per-tenant headroom reserves vs pooled headroom for utilization, 3) soft vs hard priority lanes for streaming vs turbo requests, 4) API surface: scheduler callbacks vs config-driven heuristics.

jamie: For (1) we landed on preemptive eviction for long-running microbatches only when we can guarantee a fast fallback path, otherwise we prefer admission slowdown. Eviction without a fallback caused token explosions in prod last quarter.

sri: +1. Also noted that eviction requires a robust KV-cache checkpoint/restore handshake. If we evict a request we need to carry enough prefix state to re-enqueue without a full cold start.

chris: Re: headroom: pooled headroom wins for overall throughput, but per-tenant reserves are required for enterprise SLAs. We should support both via tiered policies. Defaults = pooled, enterprise flag toggles reserved.

sam: Can we express that as a policy doc and a small proto? Something like:
```proto
message AdmissionPolicy {
  oneof mode {
    Pooled pooled = 1;
    Reserved reserved = 2;
  }
  float target_tail_ms = 10; // soft SLO
  float max_burst_tokens = 11;
}
```
That would make config-driven heuristics pluggable.

maria: I like the proto idea. It also helps the console UI. But be cautious: the scheduler should not call arbitrary customer code. Plugins are only policy descriptors, not executors.

alex: Operational concerns: metrics we need for rollout — per-tenant 95/99 latencies, eviction count, requeue rate, kvcache-miss-on-eviction, batch-formation-delay. We should add a "preempt_reasons" enum for visibility.

jamie: add a short list of integration tests too: deterministic scheduling sim with synthetic tenants (hotspot, bursty, steady), and an end-to-end where a preempted request is requeued to a cold lane to validate correctness.

sri: One more tradeoff: lane count. Fewer lanes => less queueing overhead but coarser isolation. More lanes => better isolation, worse packing. We suggested dynamic lane folding: start with N logical lanes per GPU and merge underutilized lanes after X seconds.

chris: Implementation note: dynamic folding complicates affinity and KV cache lifetime. If we merge lanes you either migrate KV caches (expensive) or accept cache coldness. We recommended migrating only metadata and rely on prefix caching to mitigate coldness.

sam: Do we want a compatibility shim for existing admission APIs? Our current enq/deq endpoints assume single queue. We'll need a thin adapter to present the multi-lane interface.

maria: yes. Adapter should be small and reversible. Plan: 1) proto + policy model 2) adapter layer 3) simulator tests 4) canary binary with metrics 5) staged rollout.

alex: timeline?

maria: aim for prototype branch in 2 weeks, simulator tests in 3, internal staging in 6, canary to 5% traffic in 10. We can tighten after initial telemetry.

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: prototype branch pushed to staging-cluster-3 at 2611800180 by chris.

chris: pushed prototype adapter and a simple pooled/reserved policy impl. No KV migration yet. Breaking it into smaller PRs.

jamie: For the simulator, I'll wire up a tenant generator to reproduce the "token explosion" bug. Need input: distributions for burstiness and sequence lengths.

maria: i'll drop the workload histograms from last month's live trace in #eng-runtime-telemetry. Use that for realistic seeds.

sam: question: what do we do about streaming requests that hold the KV cache open for long durations? They block batching. Proposed heuristic: streaming gets a soft lane with token-per-second budget and preemptible after an idle-window.

sri: Streaming also needs priority hint in request headers so the admission controller can treat them differently without changing the scheduler core. Add header X-Redwood-Stream: true with stream_timeout_ms.

alex: agree. Also add observability for streaming preemptions so product can tune end-to-end UX.

maria: action items: - sam/jamie: proto + simulator seeds (this week) - chris: adapter PRs (start now) - alex: metric dashboards (add preempt reasons) - sri: KV checkpoint handshake sketch - i'll own canary plan + rollout doc.

chris: quick note: prefer feature-flag guard for the adapter so we can flip back fast.

maria: yep feature flag on the routing layer. Also include kill-switch that routes specific tenants to legacy queue.

jamie: any objections to the dynamic lane folding approach? we should keep it experimental.

alex: experimental only. :thumbsup:

sam: I'll open the proto PR and link here.

maria: thanks all. If no blockers i'll grab the RFC follow-up doc and paste into the repo under docs/ops/scheduler-refactor.md after the prototype lands.

deploy-bot: canary rollout queued: 5% traffic -> staging-us-west on 2611800500.

maria: perfect — we'll reconvene after the simulator results.
